questions.question: Government of India accounts are kept in three parts. Which of the following is NOT one of the three?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cooperative fund**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cooperative fund** is **NOT** one of the three main funds of the Government of India.
 
• A **Cooperative Fund** generally refers to funds that are managed by **cooperative societies** or **cooperative institutions**.
 
• These funds are used for the financial management and operations of cooperative organizations, which are member-owned and operated entities aimed at mutual benefit
 
• The fund can be generated from membership fees, savings and contributions of members, profits from cooperative business activities, government grants, or loans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The accounts of the Government of India are maintained in **three parts**, which are:
 
• **Public Account**:
 
 
• This includes transactions where the government acts as a banker.
 
• It deals with funds like provident funds, small savings, etc., where the government holds money on behalf of others.
 
 
 
• **Consolidated Fund**:
 
 
• This is the most important account and contains all revenues (like taxes) and loans raised by the government.
 
• All government expenditures are made from this fund, and no amount can be withdrawn without the approval of Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Contingency Fund**:
 
 
• This fund is used to meet unforeseen expenditures.
 
• The fund is at the disposal of the President of India to make urgent payments, subject to later approval by the Parliament.

questions.question: If Seenu covers a distance of 15.5 km in 5 hours, then the distance covered by him in 6 hours is:
questions.solution:

Distance covered in 5 hours = 15.5 km

Time = 6 hours

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Speed = Distance / Time

**Calculations:**

Speed = 15.5 km / 5 hours

⇒ Speed = 3.1 km/h

Distance in 6 hours = Speed × Time

⇒ Distance in 6 hours = 3.1 km/h × 6 hours

⇒ Distance in 6 hours = 18.6 km

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

__

• The computers in a LAN connection to each other via TCP/IP ethernet or Wi-Fi.
 
• A LAN is normally exclusive to an organization, such as a school, office, association, or church.
 
 
 
• MAN:
 
 
• It stands for metropolitan area network.
 
• The word MAN refers to merging several local area networks (LANs) in a city into a single, more extensive network that may connect to a vast area network efficiently.
 
• A MAN is larger than a LAN but smaller than a WAN.

questions.question: Which of the following movements was NOT lead by Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bardoli Satyagraha, 1928**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bardoli Satyagraha (1928)
 
 
• The British government had imposed a significant increase in land revenue on farmers in Bardoli, Gujarat.
 
• This led to widespread discontent among the farmers.
 
• The Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 was led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
 
• Although Mahatma Gandhi provided support and strategic guidance, the direct leadership of the movement was under Patel. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kheda Satyagraha (1918)
 
 
• A severe famine struck the Kheda district of Gujarat, leading to crop failures and widespread poverty.
 
• The British government refused to provide any relief to the affected farmers.
 
• Gandhi arrived in Kheda to assess the situation and galvanise the farmers into action.
 
• He encouraged them to refuse to pay taxes until they received adequate relief.
 
• The Kheda Satyagraha was another victory for Gandhi.
 
• The British government was forced to grant tax relief to the farmers, demonstrating the power of non-violent resistance.
 
 
 
• Passive Resistance Campaigns (1906)
 
 
• The British government had introduced discriminatory laws against Indian immigrants in South Africa, particularly the Transvaal.
 
• These laws limited the rights of Indians and subjected them to racial segregation.
 
• Gandhi led a series of passive resistance campaigns against these discriminatory laws.
 
• He encouraged Indians to refuse to obey unjust laws and to suffer the consequences peacefully.
 
• While the passive resistance campaigns in South Africa did not immediately achieve their goals, they helped to raise awareness of the plight of Indians and laid the foundation for Gandhi's later struggles for independence in India​
 
 
 
• Quit India Movement, 1942:
 
• Mahatma Gandhi Led this movement
 
 
• The Quit India Movement was a significant mass movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi on August 8, 1942, during World War II.
 
• The primary goal was to demand an end to British rule in India. Gandhi gave the famous "Do or Die" speech in Mumbai (then Bombay), urging Indians to do everything possible, non-violently, to drive the British out of India.
 
• The movement saw widespread civil disobedience and protests, with major impacts including the arrest of Gandhi and other leaders, violent suppression by the British, and a surge in nationalist sentiment among Indians.

questions.question: A mixture contains alcohol and water in the ratio of 5 ∶ 4. If 9 litres of water is added to the mixture, the ratio of alcohol to water becomes 4 ∶ 5. Find the quantity of alcohol in the mixture.

Let the quantity of alcohol = 5x litres

Let the quantity of water = 4x litres

After adding 9 litres of water:

New quantity of water = 4x + 9 litres

New ratio:

(5x)/(4x + 9) = (4)/(5)

**Calculation:**

⇒ 5 × 5x = 4 × (4x + 9)

⇒ 25x = 16x + 36

⇒ 25x - 16x = 36

⇒ 9x = 36

⇒ x = 4

Quantity of alcohol = 5x = 5 × 4 = 20 litres

**∴ The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: The mean of three numbers is 53. The range of this data set is 28 while the difference between the two smallest numbers is 8. The greatest of the three numbers is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The mean of three numbers is 53.

The range of this data set is 28.

The difference between the two smallest numbers is 8.

**Formula used:**

Mean = (a + b + c) / 3

Range = c - a

**Calculations:**

Mean = 53

⇒ (a + b + c) / 3 = 53

⇒ a + b + c = 159

Range = 28

⇒ c - a = 28

⇒ c = a + 28

Difference between two smallest numbers = 8

⇒ b - a = 8

⇒ b = a + 8

Substitute b and c in the sum equation:

⇒ a + (a + 8) + (a + 28) = 159

⇒ 3a + 36 = 159

⇒ 3a = 123

⇒ a = 41

Now, find b and c:

b = a + 8

⇒ b = 41 + 8 = 49

c = a + 28

⇒ c = 41 + 28 = 69

**∴ The greatest of the three numbers is 69, which is option 1.**

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution of India has been influenced by the German Constitution?

options.text: Suspension of fundamental rights during Emergency

__
 
• Suspension of Fundamental Rights

 
 
• The feature of suspending Fundamental Rights during an Emergency was taken from the Weimar Constitution of Germany
 
 
 
• **Articles 352–360 :**
 
 
• These articles in Part XVIII of the Constitution outline the Emergency provisions.. 
 
 
 
• **National, State, and Financial Emergencies**
 
 
• **The Indian Constitution, like the German Constitution, has provisions for national and state emergencies, as well as financial emergencies. **
 
 
 
• The Indian Constitution was also influenced by other sources, including:
 
 
• The Nehru Report and the Cabinet Mission Plan
 
• The Universal Declaration of Human Rights
 
• Principles of natural justice
 
• Parliamentary debates
 
• Judicial decisions
 
• Conventions

• This system is a balance between a strong central government and regional or state governments.
 
• The federal system in India is **quasi-federal, meaning it is not a true federation like the United States** but has features that resemble a federal structure with a strong central authority.
 
 
 
• **Amendment of the Constitution of India:**

options.text: Some thrones are both starks and dragons.

Some thrones are not dragons but they are starks.
All starks are either thrones or dragons.

questions.solution:
**Given: **

Statement A: All dragons are starks.

Statement B: Some starks are thrones.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/53f1fc16ac0fe541aab15c9adfa28d306adec78ff7a4c692b250755f20abe9a9.png]

3. Some thrones are not dragons but they are starks. - This can be concluded since we know some starks are thrones and not all starks are dragons.

4. All starks are either thrones or dragons. - This** cannot be** concluded based on the statements given; we only know that some starks are thrones, not that all starks are covered by these two categories.

So, **"All starks are either thrones or dragons"** CANNOT be concluded from the statements.

Hence, the correct answer is **"All starks are either thrones or dragons".**
